title: Groundwater Abstraction Return Reconciliation
verdict: Proceed (pilot gates measured; package build outstanding)
dataset: Procedurally generated confined-aquifer abstraction scenes (Theis drawdown, superposition in time and space) over REAL measured USGS NWIS instantaneous groundwater-level background residuals (parameter 72019), privately re-mixed
license: Generated corpus: CC0 1.0, author-owned generator. Background source: USGS NWIS water data, US Government work in the public domain.
blocker: Package not built. Metric must be converted from corpus-pooled to the platform metric chain (group_score then mean) before grade.py is written, and the floor re-measured under that grouping.
notes: Bound to immutable controller slot batch-20260920-044727-task-001 and its exact supplied Shipd pair. Shipd was NOT opened this run (unauthenticated session); no live novelty or duplicate check was possible.
Candidate 5 for this slot. Candidates 1-4 were measured and rejected; see the controller ledger.

Task: from 28 days of 3-hourly water-level series at 8-12 observation wells, the coordinates of 6-9 registered boreholes, and each borehole's DECLARED abstraction return (7 four-day blocks), recover each borehole's ACTUAL abstraction ledger and the aquifer's log10 transmissivity and log10 storage coefficient.

Rule-1 property: the scored answer is the private abstraction scene and the private aquifer parameters. They exist in no public record, so identifying the real background hydrograph reveals nothing about the answer; at worst it removes noise.

Measured ladder on 120 held-out scenes with background families disjoint from train (394 train / 154 test real wells): oracle 1.0000, achievable ceiling with oracle aquifer parameters 0.6397, capability-matched alternating solver 0.3424, intended sample submission 0.1445, all-zeros 0.0956, weak fixed-parameter NNLS 0.0925, train-prior constant 0.0290, uniform random 0.0143, copy-the-declaration no-op 0.0000.
Ceiling minus capability = 0.2973; capability minus best trivial baseline = 0.2468. For comparison, slot candidate 3 was rejected at 0.028.

Rule 5 compliance: the first metric gave uniform random 0.1577 and an all-zero submission 0.24 through per-row rectification and a free count head. Both heads were replaced by chance-floor-relative heads referenced to the best constant rule, which drove uniform random to 0.0143 and the no-op to 0.0000.

A misdeclaration-detection head was measured and DROPPED (weight 0): on 40 held-out scenes no solver, including the capability-matched one, beat the best constant flagging rule (reference F1 0.539), so a weighted detection head would have been unreachable dead weight. It is retained as a reported diagnostic.

Rule 6 compliance: the first capability-matched solver (free-NNLS aquifer-parameter search plus sparse deconvolution) scored 0.15 and lost to an all-zero submission. The principled version (declared-anchored aquifer-parameter search, then alternating nonnegative rate recovery and local parameter refinement) scores 0.3424. The weak version was not reported as the ceiling.
Identifiability verified: with oracle aquifer parameters and noise-free observations the recovery scores 0.9805; median design-matrix condition number 931.

Runtime: capability-matched solver 6.9 s/scene, sample-grade solver 0.17 s/scene, so a 400-500 scene test split fits a 1.5 hour CPU budget with room for cheaper strategies. That spread is the intended source of score variance.

lookup_attack.threat_model: attacker holds the exact pool of 548 real NWIS residual segments, including train families, and knows the re-mixing family
lookup_attack.method: normalised max circular cross-correlation over all shifts, both time directions and both signs
lookup_attack.hardening: two-source mixing replaced by three sources with comparable random weights plus a random linear time-warp
lookup_attack.consequence: even a perfect background match removes noise only; the scored answer is the private abstraction scene
